test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The British used education as a tool to ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**strengthen colonial rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The British introduced modern education in India primarily to create a class of educated Indians who could assist in administrative tasks, thereby strengthening colonial control.
 
• The English Education Act of 1835, spearheaded by Thomas Babington Macaulay, promoted Western knowledge and English as the medium of instruction to serve colonial interests.
 
• Educated Indians were intended to act as intermediaries between the British rulers and the Indian population, ensuring smoother governance.
 
• The curriculum emphasized British history, culture, and values, aiming to instill loyalty to the colonial government and suppress any anti-colonial sentiment.
 
• This education policy created a workforce for clerical and subordinate positions in the British administration, fulfilling the economic and political needs of the Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Macaulay’s Minute (1835)**

 
 
• Thomas Babington Macaulay advocated for the promotion of English education in India, emphasizing Western literature and science over traditional Indian knowledge systems.
 
• His famous "Minute on Indian Education" argued that educating a small elite group in English would create a class of individuals "Indian in blood and color but English in taste, opinions, morals, and intellect."
 
 
 
• **Wood’s Despatch (1854)**
 
 
• Known as the "Magna Carta of English Education in India," it laid the foundation for systematic education in the country.
 
• It recommended the establishment of universities in major cities and schools across various levels, with English as the primary medium of instruction for higher education.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Colonial Education**
 
 
• Led to the emergence of a new middle class, which played a significant role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• Undermined traditional Indian education systems and cultural values.
 
• Created social divisions, as access to education was limited to a privileged few.
 
 
 
• **Downward Filtration Theory**
 
 
• It was the idea that educating a small elite group would eventually lead to the spread of knowledge and Western values to the broader population.
 
• This theory justified the limited investment in mass education by the British colonial government.
